title: MDN Curriculum: front-end developer skills
why_trusted: Mozilla's own free, self-paced curriculum on developer.mozilla.org that lists the essential front-end skills, refined with input from educators and the web community.

title: Baseline: web platform feature availability
authors: Chrome team and external experts (web.dev); WebDX Community Group
why_trusted: The web.dev page defining Baseline (Newly available when all core browsers support a feature, Widely available 30 months later), a status set by the WebDX Community Group.

title: The TC39 Process
why_trusted: Published by TC39 on its own domain; it defines Stages 0 to 4 that every JavaScript proposal passes, and Stage 4 requires two compatible implementations passing Test262.

title: State of JavaScript 2025 survey results
why_trusted: Annual open survey run by Devographics (13,002 responses, Sept 24 to Nov 10 2025, published Feb 3 2026); its About page states it is a snapshot of a self-selected subset, so use it for trends, not as proof of usage.

title: Origin trials (Chrome for Developers)
why_trusted: The Chrome team's own documentation of the origin trial program, including registration, tokens and expiry.

title: Implementing feature detection (MDN)
why_trusted: MDN Web Docs, the cross-browser reference maintained by Mozilla and partners; this guide covers @supports, CSS.supports(), the in operator and undetectable features.

title: Polyfill supply chain attack hits 100K+ sites
why_trusted: Sansec is the security firm that published the first forensic analysis of the 2024 polyfill.io supply-chain attack, with dated updates; it is used here only as evidence of that failure, not as a production-practice source.

title: preactjs/preact
why_trusted: The project itself: the Preact UI library, a React-compatible library with a compact source; MIT license; 39009 stars; the official We-are-using page names production adopters.

title: mdn/browser-compat-data
why_trusted: The machine-readable browser compatibility dataset behind MDN browser-support tables, which the Baseline data in web-platform-dx/web-features is computed from; CC0-1.0 data; stars 5794 in the specialised niche of web-platform compatibility data (tier A niche bar is 2000). Used by MDN, caniuse, WebStorm per its README.
niche_reason: Specialised niche: web-platform browser compatibility data (2000-star niche bar for tier A).

title: How to Contribute to Open Source (Open Source Guides)
why_trusted: GitHub's own Open Source Guides; its section 'Why contribute to open source?' says public contributions build a reputation and that teaching and learning go together; source repo github/opensource.guide has 15805 stars, last push 2026-11-16.

title: Can I use: About and support legend
why_trusted: The project's own site for the caniuse browser support tables. Its About page (read live in a browser on 2026-11-17 and 2026-11-18; it answers HTTP 406 to command-line fetches) gives the legend: green supported, red not supported, greenish yellow partial, gray unknown; support data comes from the Fyrd/caniuse GitHub repository (verified via its API) and usage share from StatCounter GlobalStats.

title: browserslist/browserslist
why_trusted: The project itself: the shared config of target browsers that front-end tools read; MIT, 13.6k stars, pushed 2026-11-16, and its README names Autoprefixer, Babel preset-env, postcss-preset-env and eslint-plugin-compat as users.
